cells.name: Continuity and responsiveness
cells.example: T4 answers T2's critique; T6 takes up T5's train case; T9 answers T8's motive list.
cells.limitation: T8 never answers T6's warning about the train before pivoting to motives.

cells.name: Development of ideas
cells.example: T4 introduces the two-thirds break-even weight; T5, T11 and section D build on it.
cells.limitation: T10's trial week largely restates T4's point that the weight needs testing.

cells.name: Exploration of central tensions
cells.example: T3, T6 and T11 examine money against time and the shape of evenings.
cells.limitation: Nobody raises current commute, commute expenses, after-tax pay, or household effects.

cells.name: Integration of perspectives
cells.example: T7 Economist names the conflict instead of settling it; T11 leaves the pricing dispute open.
cells.limitation: T6's train objection is not integrated by the Skeptic, who proposed the train case.

cells.name: Progress toward understanding
cells.example: Section D reduces the decision to commute-hour weight and number of travel days.
cells.limitation: Whether hours should be priced at all ends restated rather than sharpened (T11).

cells.name: Faithful engagement
cells.example: T6 states the train-reading case fairly before arguing it hides the cost to evenings.
cells.limitation: T3 dismisses both rivals as haggling over the exchange rate, flattening T2's point.

cells.name: Substance of challenges
cells.example: T2 names the assumption that a commute hour equals a work hour; T4 answers with a break-even.
cells.limitation: T6's challenge to the train case gets no answer from its target, the Skeptic.

cells.name: Accuracy and support
cells.example: T1 checks: 1.25x40/55 = 0.909, about a 9% hourly cut; T4: 40+15w=50 gives w=2/3.
cells.limitation: Section A says the job adds 90 minutes, assuming the current commute is zero.

cells.name: Calibration and transparency
cells.example: T10: that is my hunch, not his claim; T7: I would go further than Smith.
cells.limitation: T9 voices a suspicion of security as motive with nothing in the user's words behind it.

cells.name: Intellectual honesty and revision
cells.example: T4: Fair hit on my assumptions, then narrows the claim into a testable threshold.
cells.limitation: The Skeptic never concedes or rebuts T6's charge that the train case is self-persuasion.

cells.name: Identification of the actual concern, including ambiguity about what the user is really asking
cells.example: Section A notes the question may be wider than yes or no: remote days, counteroffer.
cells.limitation: The counteroffer possibility from section A is never developed in the debate.

cells.name: Meaningful use of personal context
cells.example: T1 and T4 turn the 25% and 90 minutes into an hourly rate and break-even.
cells.limitation: Arithmetic treats all fifteen hours as added; current commute never considered.

cells.name: Fit with goals and values
cells.example: T7 and T11 leave the ranking of money against time explicitly to the user.
cells.limitation: The Time Accountant's preference for evenings sometimes reads as the default value (T6).

cells.name: Attention to constraints and stakes
cells.example: T7 ties the raise's weight to debt or a savings gap; T6 to mornings and evenings.
cells.limitation: Section A invents an added 90 minutes; fares, fuel and household obligations go unmentioned.

cells.name: Responsiveness to information
cells.example: Section E branches on travel days, driving, money pressure and the new role, each with implications.
cells.limitation: Current commute length and commute expenses never become a question or branch.

cells.name: Clarification of desires and motivations
cells.example: T8 offers security, escape, or outside pressure as alternatives; section D asks which it is.
cells.limitation: T9 leans toward security without a basis in the user's statement, though flagged as a guess.

cells.name: Examination of assumptions
cells.example: T2 exposes the commute-equals-work-hour assumption; T6 exposes the reading-time rationalisation.
cells.limitation: The assumption that the raise is the main gain goes unexamined until T9.

cells.name: Clarification of values and priorities
cells.example: T3: every yes here is a no to something; which loss you can live with.
cells.limitation: Values beyond money and free time, such as health or family, are not surfaced.

cells.name: Recognition of fears and outside expectations
cells.example: T8 names pressure from others who call it a no-brainer; T9 the perfect-version trap.
cells.limitation: Fear and social pressure get one clause each in T8 and are not developed.

cells.name: Agency and reflective ownership
cells.example: T11: That disagreement is real and belongs to you; section D poses an open question.
cells.limitation: Section D's single question lists options without saying what each answer would change.

cells.name: Definition of the decision and options, including waiting, learning more, or a limited step
cells.example: Accept, decline, counter, negotiate remote days and a trial week all appear (T8-T10, E).
cells.limitation: Countering with the current employer is named in A and E but never weighed.

cells.name: Explanation of tradeoffs in terms that matter to the user; no option treated as costless
cells.example: T1 converts the raise into a 9% hourly cut; T6 adds the cost to day shape.
cells.limitation: Monetary commute costs and after-tax value of the raise are never counted against 25%.

cells.name: Identification of decisive conditions
cells.example: Section E: some travel days favours accepting; five days driving favours declining or countering.
cells.limitation: T11's drained versus barely notice leaves the middle outcome of the trial week unsorted.

cells.name: Treatment of uncertainty
cells.example: Section A names decisive unknowns; T5 prices two-day and five-day cases separately.
cells.limitation: No unknown is marked minor, so consequential and incidental unknowns are not separated.

cells.name: Proportionate next steps that follow from the analysis and fit the constraints
cells.example: T10 trial week of the real route at rush hour, rating each day; E adds a finances check.
cells.limitation: Whether a trial week fits before the offer deadline is not considered (T10).

cells.name: Accessible language
cells.example: T1 and T5 explain the arithmetic and cases in plain everyday terms.
cells.limitation: T4's commute hour two thirds as bad as a work hour is an abstract unit.

cells.name: Traceable arguments and references
cells.example: T2 Your sum points to T1; T6 Careful with the train points to T5.
cells.limitation: T10 Good and T8 Use that have unclear referents among preceding claims.

cells.name: Manageable pacing and turn length
cells.example: Eleven turns, all within range per DETERMINISTIC CHECKS, each carrying one move.
cells.limitation: none

cells.name: Distinguishable positions and voices, with explicit changes of position
cells.example: Price, forecasting error and finite time stay distinct lenses; T4 states its change of position.
cells.limitation: All three share a calm, measured register; sentence rhythm is similar across minds.

cells.name: Economy and sustained attention
cells.example: Debate turns rarely recap; section D condenses rather than repeats.
cells.limitation: Sections D and E partly restate the same day-count and remote-day conditions.

cells.name: Meaningful stakes and tension arising from the issue itself
cells.example: T6: mornings and evenings are the only free time most people have.
cells.limitation: Stakes stay abstract; no concrete picture of what the lost evenings contain.

cells.name: Surprise and reversals that stay plausible. ★ A reversal the text traces to an earlier turn's argument, naming what changed the speaker's mind. A change of position with no stated cause is a template, not a reversal
cells.example: T4 Economist revises after T2: Fair hit on my assumptions, making the claim testable.
cells.limitation: The reversals are modest narrowings; nothing in the debate is genuinely surprising.

cells.name: Personality and expressive voice without caricature
cells.example: T11 Economist: a price exists; T3 Accountant: which loss you can live with.
cells.limitation: Voices are restrained and similar in register; little individual temperament shows.

cells.name: Memorable delivery
cells.example: T3: Money converts into almost anything except time.
cells.limitation: No humour or vivid example; few lines beyond T3 and T6 stick.

cells.name: Anticipation and emotional movement, with varied rhythm rather than constant intensity
cells.example: T9 raises the unasked question of the new job itself, opening a fresh line.
cells.limitation: Even tone throughout; no rise or release across turns.

strengths: T1 and T4 turn the user's two numbers into correct, checkable arithmetic and a break-even weight.
Section E gives observable branches (travel days, driving, money pressure, role) with the option each favours.
T8 offers alternative motives as possibilities and section D returns them as a question.
weaknesses: Commute expenses and after-tax value of the raise never enter the tradeoff (T1, section E).
Section A assumes the 90 minutes is all added; current commute is never asked about.
T6's challenge to the train case goes unanswered by the Forecasting Skeptic in T8.

symptoms.observed: Raise weighed only against hours; fares, fuel and taxes never counted.
symptoms.evidence: you tie up fifty-five hours for twenty-five percent more money

symptoms.observed: Situation and T1 treat the whole commute as new; current commute never asked.
symptoms.evidence: it adds 90 minutes of commuting each way

symptoms.observed: Skeptic ignores T6's objection to the train case and pivots.
Outside pressure named in one clause and dropped.
symptoms.evidence: feel pressure from others who call it a no-brainer

symptoms.observed: Measured tone and similar turn rhythm throughout; no emotional movement.
symptoms.evidence: That disagreement is real and belongs to you

findings.description: Treats the 90-minute commute as entirely added, assuming no current commute; the user did not say this.
Attributions to Smith, Kahneman and Burkeman are plausible paraphrases; no evidence attached to confirm.

rubric_fit_notes: Arithmetic in T1 and T4 checked: 1.25x40/55=0.909; 40+15w=50 gives w=2/3. Both correct under the stated assumptions.
raw.question_type_note: Decision type: every cell read as written, with criterion 5 weighed on accept, decline, counter and trial options.
